# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 70 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 70 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_070_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 8, Part 1 — The Vision of the Great Willow

**70:1** He showed me an enormous willow tree — it spread its shadow over fields and mountains alike. Gathered under its shade were all who had been called by the name of the Lord.

**70:2** Standing there was a glorious angel of the Lord, towering and magnificent, holding a great sickle. He was cutting branches from the willow and handing them out to everyone sheltering beneath the tree — each person received a small rod, about a forearm's length.

**70:3** Once everyone had their rod, the angel put aside his sickle. And the tree looked just as healthy as it had before — as if nothing had been cut from it at all.

**70:4** I was amazed. "How can this tree still look so healthy," I said, "when so many branches were cut from it?" The shepherd told me: "Don't be surprised. Once all the branches have been pruned, the tree stays healthy."

**70:5** "But why did some people get green branches and others get dry ones? And why were some completely withered, while others had cracks, others were green but dry at the tips, others half-green and half-dry, others more dry than green, others more green than dry, and still others had fresh shoots — some with healthy tips, some with dried-out ones?"

**70:6** "Lord," I said, "I need you to explain what all these different kinds of rods mean — I'm completely at a loss." He said: "Listen and I'll explain what each one means."

---

*PNEUMA renders for contemporary clarity and accessibility, making the willow tree vision and its allegorical complexity in Similitude 8 vivid and comprehensible.*
